reviews.text: At the end of the day, it is doing too much. The political commentary feels incredibly shallow and the plot is so barely there making it hard to follow and the heist confusing...I really, really wanted to like 6 Underground but I just can’t.
reviews.author: Elizabeth Garcia

reviews.text: The structure is poorly assembled and every character is given very little emotional depth.
reviews.author: Josh Parham

reviews.text: There's a method to Bay's madness, and you'll find it crammed somewhere in-between his cuts by the millisecond and swooping low-angle camera movements.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Did Michael Bay invent World Cinema or did the world just copy him? The spectacle is savage, the metacommentary delightful, and the pace bloodthirsty though it runs long.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: I am not sure who this is for, but anyone who has the stamina to make it all the way through the end of it deserves to be eligible for financial compensation.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Bay's clumsy but visually impressive movie should partly sate anyone waiting for the superior thrills and spills of the next Fast & Furious outing.
reviews.author: Nick Levine

reviews.text: The choreography and orchestration is brilliant when you take a step back, and an exhausting adrenaline rush as you take it in.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: If you want mindless action, 6 Underground delivers the goods. Don't expect the film to be intellectually stimulating or dramatically satisfying. If you are, you have never seen a Michael Bay movie before.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Bar a couple of ridiculous sequences that stand out for their colourful design and audaciousness, the film is simply too aimless to find much of a reason to care beyond the over-stylised film-making.
reviews.author: Andrew Gaudion

reviews.text: 6 Underground is the kind of film that considers a nun giving the middle finger to be the height of edgy humour.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: In the moments that connect the action, 6 Underground becomes one of the worst, most cringeworthy movies of the last few years.
reviews.author: Justin Jones

reviews.text: A scattered grab bag of images and noises.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: 6 Underground is Mountain Dew in cinema form, bursting with energy and ridiculous ideas that is occasionally entertaining but mostly just exhausting.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: It's not clever. It's not classy. He thinks it is. But it's bold and tough, and you will respect the awesome might of military technology, else be visited in the night by wicked-rad army ninjas in stealth Blackhawks...
reviews.author: Luke Whiston

reviews.text: This is a terrible action movie that utilizes Michael Bay's worst instincts and none of his best.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: This is indeed a Michael Bay movie, and it has no shame about that. It's utterly insane-and an absolute blast.
reviews.author: Josh Martin

reviews.text: This is about as optional as it gets...it's not taking up big screens for "real cinema," but it's just there for people who know they enjoy this type of thing. It's very transparent.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: I'm not a Michael Bay fan, but despite myself, I was really enjoying this. A guilty pleasure.
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: Netflix's sorry attempt at building an action franchise goes very awry with a project that has absolutely no redeeming qualities.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: It's so over-the-top that it's oddly dull.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Reynolds has clearly been hired to deliver Deadpool-esque deadpan, which he does with aplomb.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: The result is an absurd orgy of action and comedy with no filter whatsoever. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Military idolatry and craven female objectification and a belief that the rich will save us? 6 Underground has it all!
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: 6 Underground believes in a more is more philosophy.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: It's a film that lets its audience gorge on violence and bravado, only to make us feel sick of the taste by the final reel.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: A migraine headache in cinematic form.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Explosive action, bloody images in intense adventure.
reviews.author: Renee Schonfeld

reviews.text: Before the credits roll, 6 Underground will either trigger your adrenal glands or leave you triggered.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: Leave this crew alone to make one of these every year for the next decade. "Fast and Furious" be warned, the Bay is back in town.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: Not a film for people who like their movies meaningful or to have detailed characters and plot, it is a bonanza for fans of massive action films with wisecracking characters, explosions, chases and guns.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: Here the narrative glue is set aside for the benefit of a spectacle overdose with someone behind who knows very well how to handle it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Everything in the long opening sequence of 6 Underground appeals to the unconfessable pleasure of sowing chaos. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Miguel Muñoz Garnica

reviews.text: There's something almost homey about getting this version of Bay bombast back. For anyone with affection for, say, The Rock or Bad Boys, it's a nice feeling. At first.
reviews.author: Tim Stevens

reviews.text: 6 Underground...is a loud, smug, barely comprehensible wad of action movie; the vibe is as though the entire thing was conceptualized on a cocktail napkin at whatever place exists on the spectrum between a Hooters and a strip club.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Can't see it? Who cares. Can't feel it? Middle finger to you. No questions? Here's more pyrotechnics to fill up the screen and semi-naked girls to push things along. Again, just because.
reviews.author: Nguyên Lê

reviews.text: Fans of extravagant action movies will certainly have a great time, however, behind the elegant stimuli on the surface, many questionable elements shine. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Maybe you need to have some level of intoxication to truly enjoy this.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: 6 Underground really is as terrible as you'd expect it to be, exactly the kind of brainless, bombastic and seizure-inducing fare Michael Bay is known for.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: There's nothing worse than a dull action movie. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: The madman director's Netflix debut "6 Underground" is so big it feels like it's going to smash out of your television screen.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: There are scenes in 6 Underground that fail to carry their emotional weight because of their poor execution.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: 6 Underground is like a refutation of the very concept of cinema itself; this is not a negative criticism. Rather than a deconstruction, it feels like a raw vivisection of action movies, examining what blockbusters & audiences expect/need from each other
reviews.author: VyceVictus

reviews.text: Michael Bay's Netflix dud is even less coherent than the worst of his Transformers movies.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: For better and worse, in a multiplex or on your television or tablet, it delivers pleasure through pain.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: The result is the cinematic equivalent of a bad hangover.
reviews.author: Miles Surrey

reviews.text: Bay has delivered his lightest and most enjoyable movie since 2005's The Island. But this is still a Michael Bay movie, meaning it's loud, obnoxious, immature and occasionally incoherent.
reviews.author: Jon Winkler

reviews.text: What kills me most, however, is that amid all the cacophony, there's one joke that hints at the kind of joyful mayhem Bay is capable of.
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: [Michael Bay] knows that there are few things more effective in cinema than broken glass, water, blue light, [and] metal. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: The movie is messy.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: Like a live-action "Team America: World Police." It's not the best thing Michael Bay has directed, but not quite the worst either.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Hate-watch it if you must, but have your air freshener holstered and ready, and prepare yourself for a scalding-hot shower after.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Though not without its amusing moments, Michael Bay's latest is too chaotically edited and scattershot to realise its grandiose potential.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: Bay at his most obnoxious, gratuitously violent, slow-mo indulgent self. But man, does he know how to make a check your brain at the door stupidly fun action movie.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: With more explosions and non-sensical plot points than any movie he (Michael Bay) has ever made, 6 Underground is another fun action romp.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: A "Why can't things just WORK, damn it!?" save-the-world daydream processed through a lens of pure, unrestrained Bayhem; espousing what can only described - without prejudice! - as a benevolently-fascist (SMALL-f!) fantasy of utopian philanthrocapitalism.
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: Stupid. Offensive. Generally indefensible. Glorious. Another of Michael Bay's distinctly prodigious entertainments in which he continues to outdo himself & it's as much his own meditation as "The Irishman" was for Scorsese or "Roma" was for Cuarón.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: 6 Underground boasts (or suffers from) an exceedingly broad sensibility that's reflected in its myriad of garish attributes...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The second half dips into problematic territory, with a rich white savior who seems more interested in fixing one problem instead of the root cause.
reviews.author: Natalie Zutter

reviews.text: Michael Bay's signature mayhem is on full display, but beyond one single concept involving magnets, none of it in "6 Underground" impresses.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: '6 Underground' deserves to be buried alive.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Guns. Ferraris. Parkour. Headshots. Mélanie Laurent. Las Vegas. Luxury yachts. Thong underwear. Incoherence. Xenophobia. Sexism. Auteurism (Vulgar). 'Merica.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: By being exceedingly stupid, morally depraved, and dreadfully dull, "6 Underground" pulls off a hat-trick of Very Bad Filmmaking.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: ... one of Bay's better efforts to date, and a reminder that he remains an audience pull for a reason.
reviews.author: Cain Noble-Davies

reviews.text: Allowing Michael Bay to abuse the creative freedom that Netflix prides itself on offering its directors is like handing a convicted arsonist a gallon of gasoline.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: 6 Underground is Michael Bay by way of Neveldine and Taylor.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: It's a bad movie, and very outdated thanks to Michael Bay. But it's also very watchable thanks to a game cast, thrilling action sequences and beautiful locations.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Not because of the pointless noise, the bad writing or the weird tacit endorsement of the military-industrial complex, but because I was worried I wouldn't be able to articulate just how bad the film is and how intensely unpleasant it is to watch...
reviews.author: Thomas Barrie

reviews.text: Michael Bay shows he's a dusty relic by trying to create a hit film for teenage boys in 2005.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: Ryan Reynolds classes up the joint in a Michael Bay film that's an argument both for and against the Sokovia Accords.
reviews.author: Matt Fowler

reviews.text: The film is a pure expression of the id for a filmmaker who thrives on moving at 100 cuts per second; for everyone else, as the expression goes, your mileage may vary.
reviews.author: Marshall Shaffer

reviews.text: If you like your Bayhem pure and unfiltered, this one's for you. Others need not apply.
reviews.author: Amon Warmann

reviews.text: Offers no surprises or thrills as Bay paints by numbers to deliver product, not cinema, finally reaching the self-parody phase of his career.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The king of excessive action cinema has returned. Long live the king. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rubén Romero Santos

reviews.text: An expensive, incoherent dud that'll try the patience of any viewer.
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: It's an entertainingly goofy and excessive folly from Bay.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: If Michael Bay is going to continue to use his Netflix clout to bring talents like Melanie Laurent to American audiences, then l say we can find a silver lining to pretty much any film.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: There are genuinely eccentric innovations here. There's certainly not a whole lot of recognizable humanity, but hey, that's why there's "It's a Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood."
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

reviews.text: It's the Bay-iest Michael Bay movie ever. Whether that's a good or bad thing entirely depends on your tolerance level for Bayhem.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: Filmmaker Michael Bay, known for excess and imagery above all else, delivers his signature brand of sophomoric spectacle with 6 Underground.
reviews.author: Ed Travis

reviews.text: What he seems to be chasing is the feeling of freedom, the windswept open-skies exhilaration of a man who has everything. But he's still just doing donuts, hoping all those whiplash turns from nihilism to macho sentiment awaken something inside him.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: 6 Underground feels twice as disappointing for its early success.
reviews.author: Matthew Monagle

reviews.text: Overblown, outrageous, exceedingly violent and visually exhausting, director Michael Bay's latest is also kind of dumb; pretty much what you'd expect despite its strong cast.
reviews.author: Kim Hughes

reviews.text: Every single thing about 6 Underground is excessive. There are helicopters in just about every scene. Every scene seems to take place at golden hour. The violence is unspeakably gruesome, and it's constant.
reviews.author: Liam Mathews

reviews.text: After a strong start the movie steadily declines, one set piece after another, and there are many moments where the mind wanders and then asks: "Is this still going on?"
reviews.author: Mark Olsen

reviews.text: 6 Underground... is a riotous and gleefully delirious assault on the senses. It is vulgar. It is absurd. And it is completely enthralling.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: 6 Underground proves so uneven in its tone and unrelenting in its volume that it's hard to imagine a hole deep enough in which to bury its silliness.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: It delivers on its promise to be the most Michael Bay movie yet. Make of that what you will.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: It becomes repetitive, nonsensical, and just loud after everyone gets an origin story and we're left with nothing to do but go boom.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: 6 Underground is too incomprehensible to be fun and too mean to be likable.
reviews.author: Evan Saathoff

reviews.text: It wouldn't be a Michael Bay movie if he didn't slavishly cater to the lowest common denominator (get ready for some sexist and gay-panic jokes!), so it makes sense that Bay's antiheroes are more obnoxious when they're trying to be good.
reviews.author: Simon Abrams

reviews.text: Even if the film constantly risks collapsing under its weight due to constant "Bayhem," 6 Underground still has the feel of a movie belonging uniquely to one filmmaker.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: "6 Underground," a non-stop stunt reel with a few, admittedly impressive displays of your usual visual verve -- is just "Fast & Furious" crossed with an old Whitesnake music video, but with fewer functioning brain cells.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: Excessive, wanton, gorgeous, bizarre.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Reynolds should have stopped going underground after 'Buried.'
reviews.author: John DeFore

reviews.text: It's pure Bay, through and through.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: If you can get past the imbecilic script, there's no question that Bay has seized the opportunity to make "6 Underground" as visually stunning as such a project can withstand.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: It all comes together in the end, as 6 Underground is operating with a higher tally of good ideas versus bad ideas, but as its all playing out it feels consistently on the brink of falling apart.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

synopsis: Six individuals from all around the globe, each the very best at what they do, have been chosen not only for their skill, but for a unique desire to delete their pasts to change the future.
